purpose: Levocarnitine is used to treat low levels of carnitine in your body, which can happen naturally or because of certain medical conditions like kidney disease. Your body needs carnitine to turn fat into energy that your muscles and organs can use. It is also used in people on dialysis who lose carnitine during their treatments.
how_it_works: Think of carnitine as a shuttle bus inside your body. It picks up fatty acids and carries them into the part of your cells that burns fat for energy. Without enough carnitine, fat cannot get into that energy-burning area, so your body feels tired and weak. This medication replenishes your carnitine levels so that process can work properly again.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, or diarrhea are the most common side effects. Some people notice a fishy body odor, which is harmless but can be bothersome. These effects are usually mild and often improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have seizures, because levocarnitine may increase seizure activity in some people. If you have kidney disease or are on dialysis, your doctor will carefully adjust your dose. Do not use supplements or forms of carnitine that are not prescribed, as the wrong form (D-carnitine) can actually block how levocarnitine works in your body.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual oral dose is 990 mg (one tablet or 10 mL of liquid) two to three times a day with meals. For people on dialysis, it is often given as an injection into the IV line after each dialysis session. Your doctor will decide the exact dose that is right for you based on your condition and lab results.
